rules.p: Être and avoir follow no pattern; learn their six forms by heart. They build most of the rest of the language.

ex.en: Are you tired? Yes, I'm sleepy.

rules.p: Before a vowel, je drops its e: je suis → j'ai, j'étais, j'aurai.

ex.en: I have a question.

rules.p: parler → je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. About 90% of verbs work this way.

ex.en: We speak French at home.

rules.p: il parle and ils parlent sound identical. The endings are spelling, not sound; listen for nous and vous instead.

ex.en: They live in Lyon.

rules.h: Learn the top ten as words
rules.p: aller, faire, prendre, venir, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir, voir, dire are irregular and everywhere. Memorize each as a whole word, not a pattern.

ex.fr: Je vais au marché et je prends du pain.
ex.en: I'm going to the market and getting bread.

rules.p: In many irregulars, nous and vous revert to the infinitive stem: je viens, tu viens, il vient, but nous venons, vous venez.

ex.fr: Ils viennent ce soir ; nous, nous venons demain.
ex.en: They're coming tonight; we're coming tomorrow.

rules.p: se lever → je me lève, tu te lèves, il se lève, nous nous levons, vous vous levez, ils se lèvent.

ex.en: I get up at seven.

rules.p: Many verbs take the pronoun even though English doesn't: s'appeler, se lever, se coucher, se rappeler.

ex.en: Her name is Léa.

rules.p: With a plural subject the same form reads 'each other': nous nous aimons, ils s'écrivent. With a thing as subject it reads passive: ce livre se vend bien.

ex.fr: Nous nous aimons ; ce livre se vend bien.
ex.en: We love each other; this book sells well.

t3.exc: Some verbs exist only with se: se souvenir, s'en aller, il se peut que = maybe.

rules.p: être en train de + infinitive points at this exact moment. The plain present covers both now and habitually; this pins it to now.

ex.fr: Je suis en train de cuisiner, je te rappelle.
ex.en: I'm cooking right now, I'll call you back.

rules.p: The near future works like English 'going to'. aller conjugates, the main verb stays an infinitive.

ex.fr: On va voir un film ce soir.
ex.en: We're going to watch a film tonight.

rules.p: Futur proche sounds decided or imminent; futur simple sounds predicted or distant. Tonight's plans take futur proche.

ex.en: It's going to rain, take your umbrella.

rules.p: Aller in the imparfait + infinitive = was about to. The plan was set, then something interrupted it.

ex.fr: Il allait partir quand elle est arrivée.
ex.en: He was about to leave when she arrived.

rules.p: 'Just did it'. venir conjugates, de stays, the action stays an infinitive.

ex.en: I've just finished my homework.

rules.p: For 'had just', venir moves to the imparfait: je venais de finir. Never the passé composé of venir for this meaning.

ex.fr: Il venait de partir quand elle est arrivée.
ex.en: He had just left when she arrived.

rules.p: Passé composé = avoir or être in the present + the participle. Regular participles: parler → parlé, finir → fini, vendre → vendu.

ex.en: I ate and she left.

rules.p: It says what happened and moved on: what you did, not how things were.

ex.en: Yesterday we visited the museum.

rules.p: Take the tu, nous or vous present form and drop the pronoun: parle ! parlons ! parlez !

ex.en: Listen carefully and repeat.

rules.p: être → sois, soyons, soyez. avoir → aie, ayons, ayez. savoir → sache, sachons, sachez.

ex.en: Be nice to the cat!

rules.p: -er verbs and aller drop the tu -s: parle ! va ! But it comes back before y and en: vas-y, parles-en.

ex.en: Don't hesitate, go on!

rules.p: Attach the reflexive pronoun after the verb: lève-toi, levons-nous, levez-vous. The negative wraps normally: ne te lève pas.

ex.en: Get up!

rules.h: Past imperative: aie fini, sois parti
rules.p: avoir or être imperative + participle orders an action done by a deadline. Formal register only — speech uses the present imperative plus a deadline.

ex.en: Be back before midnight.

rules.p: The conditionnel of vouloir, pouvoir and aimer turns requests into polite ones.

ex.fr: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
ex.en: I'd like a coffee, please.

rules.p: pouvoir in the conditionnel makes questions softer than pouvez-vous.

ex.en: Could you help me, please?

rules.p: pouvoir = can, vouloir = want, devoir = must. Each sits straight before an infinitive.

ex.en: I want to learn, but I have to work.

rules.p: je peux, je veux, je dois; ils peuvent, ils veulent, ils doivent. You will use these more than most regular verbs.

ex.en: They can come at eight.

rules.p: il faut + infinitive = it's necessary to. The il never changes and nothing agrees with anything.

ex.en: You have to book ahead.

rules.p: With a person and a noun, il faut becomes 'need': il me faut du temps.

ex.en: I need five minutes.

rules.p: pour + infinitive = in order to. It explains a purpose.

ex.en: I'm here to learn.

rules.p: pour + noun gives a beneficiary; pour + infinitive gives a goal.

ex.en: A gift for Marie.

rules.p: -tion, -té, -ure, -ette lean feminine; -age, -ment, -eau, -isme lean masculine. The rest is memory.

ex.en: the nation, the cheese.

rules.h: Learn the article as part of the word
rules.p: Memorize 'une table', never 'table'. You can't use the noun without its gender anyway.

ex.en: It's an idea, it's a problem.

t13.exc: -age is masculine except la page, la plage, la cage, l'image, la nage, la rage.

rules.p: Most plurals add a silent -s; singular and plural sound the same. -al goes to -aux: journal → journaux.

ex.en: a horse, horses.

rules.p: bijou, caillou, chou, genou, hibou, joujou, pou take -x. Every other -ou word takes -s.

ex.en: pebbles and cabbages.

rules.p: le, la, les point at something known; un, une, des introduce something new.

ex.en: I have a dog. The dog is called Rex.

rules.p: le and la become l' before a vowel, but les never elides. de + le = du, à + le = au, à + les = aux, de + les = des.

ex.fr: C'est l'ami du voisin, le chien des voisins.
ex.en: That's the neighbour's friend, the neighbours' dog.

rules.p: Abstract and mass nouns take le/la where English uses nothing: le bonheur, le lait, la musique.

ex.en: Music is important.

rules.p: For stuff you don't count: du pain, de la confiture, des pâtes. Before a vowel it's de l': de l'eau. English often skips the article; French never does.

ex.fr: Je prends du café, elle boit de l'eau.
ex.en: I have coffee, she drinks water.

rules.p: In the negative, du, de la and des all collapse to de.

ex.en: There's no milk left.

rules.p: aimer, préférer and adorer keep the definite article, even in the negative: je n'aime pas le café.

ex.en: I don't like black coffee.

t16.exc: Quantity words also take de: beaucoup de pain, une tasse de café.

rules.p: Feminine adds -e, plural adds -s: un petit garçon, une petite fille, des petites filles.

ex.en: She's happy, they're happy.

rules.p: One male in a group and the whole group goes masculine plural.

ex.en: Marc and Léa are short.

rules.p: bon → bonne, nouveau → nouvelle, vieux → vieille, beau → belle, blanc → blanche, frais → fraîche. A masculine already ending in -e doesn't move: rouge stays rouge.

ex.en: a beautiful day, a red table.

t17.exc: Noun and compound colours never agree: des robes marron, orange, bleu marine — but rose agrees: des robes roses. beau, nouveau, vieux take bel, nouvel, vieil before a vowel: un bel homme, un vieil ami.

rules.h: Most follow, a short band leads
rules.p: Most adjectives follow the noun. Beauty, age, goodness and size go before: beau, joli, jeune, vieux, nouveau, bon, mauvais, meilleur, grand, petit, gros, long.

ex.en: a big house, a red car.

rules.p: un grand homme = a great man; un homme grand = a tall man. ancien, cher and propre behave the same way.

ex.en: my former teacher / an antique piece of furniture.

rules.p: la semaine dernière = last week, la dernière semaine = the final one of a series. seul before the noun = only, after it = alone. Two trailing adjectives join with et; des shrinks to de before a pre-placed adjective (de grandes maisons).

ex.fr: la semaine dernière / la dernière semaine ; une robe verte et bleue.
ex.en: last week / the final week; a green and blue dress.

rules.h: Match the thing, not the owner
rules.p: mon, ma, mes agree with the noun that follows. son livre can be his book or her book.

ex.en: my sister and her friends.

rules.p: Before a vowel, feminine nouns borrow mon, ton, son: mon amie, ton école.

ex.en: My school is big.

rules.p: ce before a consonant, cet before a vowel, cette for feminine, ces for plural. One set for near and far.

ex.en: this apartment, this kitchen.

rules.h: très boosts adjectives, beaucoup boosts verbs
rules.p: très grand works, beaucoup grand does not. j'aime beaucoup works, j'aime très does not.

ex.en: This cake is very good, I like it a lot.

rules.p: trop + adjective, trop de + noun.

ex.fr: C'est trop cher et il y a trop de monde.
ex.en: It's too expensive and there are too many people.

rules.p: assez = quite, peu = not very, before an adjective. Verbs compare with autant que, not aussi: il travaille autant que moi.

ex.fr: C'est assez bon, et il travaille autant que moi.
ex.en: It's quite good, and he works as much as I do.

rules.p: lent → lente → lentement; an adjective ending in a mute -e adds -ment directly (vraiment); -ant and -ent give -amment and -emment (évidemment). Irregulars: bon → bien, mauvais → mal.

ex.en: She listens attentively, obviously.

rules.p: After the verb they modify (elle écoute attentivement), before an adjective or another adverb (très intelligent), and between auxiliary and participle in compound tenses (elle a bien mangé). Several adverbs stack manner, place, time.

ex.fr: Elle a bien mangé ; il court rapidement dans le parc le matin.
ex.en: She ate well; he runs quickly in the park in the morning.

rules.p: on replaces nous in everyday speech and conjugates like il: on va, on est, on mange.

ex.en: Shall we go?

rules.p: tu for friends, family and children; vous for strangers, teachers and groups. Unsure? vous.

ex.en: What's your name? (formal)

rules.p: Weather, time and general statements use a dummy il: il pleut, il est trois heures, il faut. ils covers any group with one male; elles only all-female groups.

ex.en: It's raining, it's three o'clock.

rules.p: moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles stand alone, follow c'est, or follow a preposition.

ex.en: It's me. Come with us!

rules.p: ne before the conjugated verb, pas after. In casual speech the ne often falls silent.

ex.en: I don't understand.

rules.p: jamais = never, plus = anymore. They take pas's slot: je ne mange jamais de viande.

ex.en: She doesn't go out in the evenings anymore.

rules.p: ne pas wraps the infinitive itself, not the governing verb: je préfère ne pas partir.

ex.en: I prefer not to leave.

rules.p: Intonation: tu viens ? est-ce que: est-ce que tu viens ? inversion: viens-tu ?

ex.en: Are you coming with us?

rules.p: Intonation is casual, inversion is formal, est-ce que sits safely in the middle.

ex.en: Where do you live? (formal)

rules.p: A vowel-final verb takes a -t- bridge: va-t-il, parle-t-elle. Noun subjects stay in front: Marie vient-elle ? And je never inverts — use est-ce que je.

ex.fr: Où habite-t-elle ? Marie vient-elle ? Est-ce que je parle bien ?
ex.en: Where does she live? Is Marie coming? Do I speak well?

rules.p: qui = who, que or quoi = what, où = where, quand = when, comment = how, pourquoi = why, combien = how much.

ex.en: When are we leaving? Tomorrow.

rules.p: que opens the question and shrinks to qu' before a vowel; quoi takes over after a preposition and stands alone in casual speech.

ex.en: What do you want? What are you doing?

rules.p: When 'what' is the subject of its own question, it's qu'est-ce qui. combien takes de before a noun: combien de temps.

ex.fr: Qu'est-ce qui se passe ? Combien de temps ça prend ?
ex.en: What's happening? How long does it take?

rules.p: After savoir, demander, dire, no inversion — and que becomes ce que: je ne sais pas ce que tu veux.

ex.en: Tell me where you live.

rules.h: il y a = there is / there are
rules.p: One form for singular and plural, and il y avait for the past.

ex.en: Is there any bread?

rules.p: voilà presents something you can see arriving; c'est names or labels it.

ex.en: There's the bus! It's ours.

rules.p: With a noun or a modified noun, c'est. With a bare adjective about a person, il est.

ex.en: It's a good film. He's talented.

rules.p: Use il or elle when the subject is already in play; c'est when you label or announce.

ex.fr: Qui est-ce ? C'est Marie. Elle est là.
ex.en: Who is it? It's Marie. She's here.

rules.p: dans = in (from now), depuis = for or since (still going), il y a = ago.

ex.en: I've lived here for three years.

rules.p: French stays in the present with depuis; English switches to have + participle.

ex.en: He's been working for two hours.

rules.h: à = at, de = from, dans = inside
rules.p: à Paris, de Lyon, dans la chambre. Countries: en with feminine or vowel-initial names (en France, en Iran), au with masculine consonant ones (au Portugal, au Canada), aux with plurals (aux États-Unis).

ex.fr: Je rentre dans la maison, je viens de la boulangerie.
ex.en: I'm going back into the house, I'm coming from the bakery.

rules.p: Coming from a country mirrors the à-side: de France (feminine or vowel), du Canada, des États-Unis. vers = toward, direction without arrival.

ex.fr: Je reviens de France et je marche vers la gare.
ex.en: I'm coming back from France and walking toward the station.

rules.h: à for clocks, en for periods
rules.p: à huit heures, en mars, en 2024, le lundi for every Monday, du lundi au vendredi.

ex.en: We're leaving in June, at six.

rules.p: et = and, ou = or, mais = but, alors = so or then. They join clauses without commas.

ex.fr: Je voudrais un thé ou un café, mais sans lait.
ex.en: I'd like tea or coffee, but no milk.

rules.p: Every verb takes avoir except the être band and pronominals.

ex.en: She bought a car.

rules.p: finir → fini. Regular -re verbs drop the re and add -u: attendre → attendu, vendre → vendu, rendre → rendu. Two irregular families: prendre → pris (apprendre, comprendre, reprendre), mettre → mis (permettre, promettre).

ex.fr: J'ai attendu, puis j'ai pris le bus.
ex.en: I waited, then took the bus.

rules.p: eu, été, fait, pris, mis, vu, dit, su, voulu, pu, dû, bu, lu — most compound tenses lean on these. Used as an adjective, the participle agrees like one: une table cassée.

ex.fr: Il a pris son temps et a bu son café ; une lettre écrite à la main.
ex.en: He took his time and drank his coffee; a handwritten letter.

rules.p: Seventeen verbs of coming, going and staying take être: aller, arriver, descendre, devenir, entrer, monter, mourir, naître, partir, passer, rentrer, rester, retourner, revenir, sortir, tomber, venir. Every prefixed cousin follows its parent: redevenir, repartir, ressortir.

ex.en: They left at dawn.

rules.p: With être the participle works like an adjective: elle est allée, elles sont allées.

ex.en: Marie went up with her suitcases.

rules.p: Each verb drags its preposition: aller à Paris, venir de Lyon, entrer dans la maison, sortir du cinéma. aller moves away from the speaker, venir toward. sortir crosses a boundary out; partir is the departure itself.

ex.fr: Je vais au marché, tu viens ? Il sort de la voiture et part pour Lyon.
ex.en: I'm going to the market, coming? He gets out of the car and leaves for Lyon.

t34.exc: monter, descendre, rentrer, retourner, sortir and passer take avoir when a direct object follows: j'ai monté les valises, j'ai retourné les crêpes, j'ai passé une heure là-bas.

rules.p: Take the nous form of the present, drop -ons, add -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Only être misbehaves: ét-.

ex.en: We sang, you sang.

rules.p: Descriptions, habits, weather, feelings, background. Anything that lasted without a deadline.

ex.fr: Quand j'étais petit, il y avait un parc ici.
ex.en: When I was little, there was a park here.

rules.p: Imparfait paints the scene: weather, age, mood. Passé composé moves the plot: what happened next.

ex.en: It was raining when I went out.

rules.p: An uncounted habit with toujours or chaque été takes imparfait; a counted series of events takes passé composé.

ex.fr: Chaque été nous allions à la mer ; un jour, nous avons pris le train.
ex.en: Every summer we went to the sea; one day we took the train.

rules.p: savoir, croire, vouloir, pouvoir, aimer describe states and default to imparfait. The passé composé marks the moment the state begins: j'ai su = I found out.

ex.fr: Je savais la réponse ; quand j'ai su la vérité, j'ai pleuré.
ex.en: I knew the answer; when I learned the truth, I cried.

rules.h: A closed span takes passé composé
rules.p: pendant + a measured, finished span → passé composé: j'ai habité à Paris pendant deux ans (it's over). Open description with no endpoint → imparfait: j'habitais à Paris.

ex.fr: J'ai habité à Paris pendant deux ans.
ex.en: I lived in Paris for two years.

rules.p: parler → je parlerai, finir → je finirai. Endings: -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont.

ex.en: You'll see, everything will be fine.

rules.p: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, venir → viendr-, tenir → tiendr-, voir → verr-, savoir → saur-, pouvoir → pourr-, vouloir → voudr-, devoir → devr-, recevoir → recevr-, envoyer → enverr-, courir → courr-, mourir → mourr-, valoir → vaudr-, acquérir → acquerr-; falloir → il faudra, pleuvoir → il pleuvra.

ex.fr: J'aurai le temps, je ferai ça demain.
ex.en: I'll have time, I'll do that tomorrow.

rules.p: After quand, lorsque, dès que pointing at the future, French uses the futur where English keeps the present.

ex.en: When you arrive, call me.

t37.exc: appeler and jeter double their consonant: j'appellerai, je jetterai.

rules.p: décider de, penser à, rêver de, s'intéresser à, avoir besoin de. The preposition is part of the verb; learn the pair.

ex.en: She dreams of travelling.

rules.p: je commence à travailler, j'ai peur de voler, il continue à manger.

ex.en: It started to rain.

rules.h: A few verbs bridge with en
rules.p: croire en (believe in) and avoir confiance en. And jouer splits: jouer à = games and sports, jouer de = instruments.

ex.fr: Je crois en toi ; je joue au foot et du piano.
ex.en: I believe in you; I play football and the piano.

t38.exc: Same verb, different bridge, different meaning: penser à quelqu'un (think of someone) vs penser de (have an opinion about).

rules.p: plus rapide que, aussi rapide que, moins rapide que. The adjective sits in the middle, que does the comparing.

ex.fr: Le train est plus rapide que le bus.
ex.en: The train is faster than the bus.

rules.p: meilleur = better, pire = worse. Plus bon doesn't exist; plus mauvais exists but pire is the usual choice. bien compares with mieux, never plus bien.

ex.en: He sings better than me.

rules.p: de plus en plus = more and more, de moins en moins = less and less, fixed order, before the adjective.

ex.en: It's more and more difficult.

rules.p: le plus grand, la plus petite, les moins chers. The article turns the comparative into a superlative.

ex.fr: C'est la meilleure pâtisserie de la ville.
ex.en: It's the best bakery in town.

rules.h: bon → le meilleur, mauvais → le pire
rules.p: The irregular pair carries into the superlative.

ex.fr: C'est le pire jour de ma vie.
ex.en: It's the worst day of my life.

rules.p: me, te, le, la, nous, vous, les stand before the conjugated verb: je vois Marie → je la vois.

ex.fr: Tu connais Léa ? Oui, je la connais.
ex.en: Do you know Léa? Yes, I know her.

rules.h: me te nous vous come first
rules.p: Before le la les: il me le donne. In the passé composé the pronoun climbs before the auxiliary.

ex.en: She gave it to me yesterday.

rules.p: à Paul → lui, à mes parents → leur. lui covers him and her alike.

ex.fr: Je téléphone à Paul → je lui téléphone.
ex.en: I'm calling Paul → I'm calling him.

rules.p: Téléphoner à, parler à, écrire à, offrir à. If there's no à, you need a direct pronoun.

ex.en: I wrote them a card.

rules.h: me, te, nous, vous go both ways
rules.p: First and second persons use one pronoun for direct and indirect: il me voit, il me parle. lui and leur exist only in the third person.

ex.en: He sees me and he speaks to me.

rules.p: du pain → j'en prends, de l'espoir → j'en ai. If the phrase runs on de, en can stand in for the noun.

ex.fr: Tu veux du café ? J'en veux bien.
ex.en: Want some coffee? I'd love some.

rules.p: After a number or quantity, en holds the counted noun's place: j'en veux deux, il y en a beaucoup.

ex.en: I bought three.

rules.p: y replaces any location phrase: à + place (je vais à Paris → j'y vais), but also dans, sur, chez (chez le médecin → j'y vais). It also covers verbs that take à + thing, like penser à and croire à.

ex.fr: Tu vas au marché ? J'y vais maintenant.
ex.en: Are you going to the market? I'm on my way there.

rules.p: For à + person, keep à with a stressed pronoun: je pense à toi stays.

ex.fr: Je vais à la banque, puis j'y retire de l'argent.
ex.en: I'm going to the bank, then I'll withdraw money there.

rules.p: on replaces nous in speech, makes generic statements (on ne sait jamais), and even means 'you' in recipes and instructions.

ex.en: Shall we meet at eight?

rules.p: on a, on est, and in the negative on n'a pas, on n'est pas.

ex.en: We have no choice.

rules.p: qui is the subject (l'homme qui parle), que is the object (le film que j'ai vu), où is place or time (la ville où je suis né).

ex.fr: la femme qui chante, la chanson que j'aime.
ex.en: the woman who sings, the song I love.

rules.p: Before a vowel, drop the e: le film qu'on a vu.

ex.en: the book she's reading.

rules.h: le mien, la tienne, les siens
rules.p: The standalone possessive agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: ma voiture → la mienne.

ex.fr: Tu prends ta voiture ou la mienne ?
ex.en: Are you taking your car or mine?

rules.p: notre → le nôtre, votre → le vôtre, leur → le leur. Everyone else is plain: le mien, la tienne, les siens.

ex.fr: Notre maison est plus grande que la vôtre.
ex.en: Our house is bigger than yours.

rules.p: tout, toute, tous, toutes modify a noun and agree with it: tous les enfants, toute la journée.

ex.en: all the children, the whole day.

rules.p: Before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant, tout agrees: toute contente, toutes contentes. Before a vowel it stays put: tout étonnée.

ex.en: She's quite happy but quite surprised.

rules.p: Ils sont venus tous keeps the s sound; tous les jours drops it.

ex.en: They all came; every day.

rules.p: ça is the spoken all-purpose 'it / that'. cela is the same word dressed up for writing; ceci points at the closer thing.

ex.en: Does that work for tomorrow?

rules.h: celui, celle, ceux, celles = the one(s)
rules.p: Standalone 'the one / the ones', agreeing with the noun it replaces. celui-ci = this one, celui-là = that one. Never point at a person with ceci or cela — use the celui series.

ex.fr: Mes clés ? Prends celles de la cuisine.
ex.en: My keys? Take the ones from the kitchen.

rules.p: Free relative, people or things: celui qui travaille gagne. With a plural predicate, c'est becomes ce sont: ce sont eux.

ex.en: The one who works wins. It's them.

rules.p: plus = anymore, rien = nothing, personne = no one. They take pas's slot after the verb.

ex.en: I have no money left.

rules.p: As subjects they come first, and ne still guards the verb: personne ne sait, rien n'a changé.

ex.en: Nobody understands.

rules.p: Two negatives in one sentence intensify: je ne comprends jamais rien, personne n'a plus rien. Unlike English, they never make a positive.

ex.en: I never understand anything.

rules.p: Que c'est beau ! Comme il pleut ! Both boost a whole clause.

ex.en: How beautiful this city is!

rules.p: quel agrees with the noun it boosts: quelle idée ! quelles vacances !

ex.en: What a surprise!

rules.p: The cause clause follows the result: je reste parce qu'il pleut.

ex.en: I'm staying because it's raining.

rules.p: donc announces the consequence: il pleut, donc je reste. car is a softer cause, tacked on after a comma.

ex.en: It's raining, so I'm staying.

rules.p: It answers 'what for?' When a new person enters the aim, graduate to pour que + subjunctive (B1).

ex.en: I came to help you.

rules.p: mais joins opposites; pourtant concedes one: c'est loin, pourtant on y va.

ex.en: It's far, yet we're going.

rules.p: d'abord = first, puis or ensuite = then, enfin = finally.

ex.fr: D'abord on mange, ensuite on joue, enfin on dort.
ex.en: First we eat, then we play, finally we sleep.

rules.p: Imparfait of avoir or être + participle: j'avais mangé, j'étais parti. For an action already done before another past one.

ex.fr: Quand je suis arrivé, ils avaient déjà mangé.
ex.en: When I arrived, they had already eaten.

rules.p: Descriptions and states take imparfait; events take passé composé, or passé simple in writing.

ex.fr: La nuit tombait quand le téléphone a sonné.
ex.en: Night was falling when the phone rang.

rules.p: Anything that happened before your story's timeline gets plus-que-parfait.

ex.fr: Elle avait oublié ses clés, donc elle attendait dehors.
ex.en: She had forgotten her keys, so she waited outside.

rules.h: avoir agrees when the object goes first
rules.p: The participle agrees with a direct object placed before the verb: les fleurs que j'ai achetées, je les ai vues.

ex.en: the letters she wrote.

rules.p: j'ai écrit des lettres stays put. Only a preposed object (relative que or an object pronoun) triggers agreement.

ex.en: I saw them (them = women) yesterday.

rules.p: je parlerais, je finirais. Take the futur stem and hang the imparfait endings on it: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient.

ex.en: I'd like a glass of water.

rules.h: The stems copy the futur simple
rules.p: Every irregular futur stem carries over: je serais, j'aurais, j'irais, je ferais, je viendrais, je verrais, je saurais, je pourrais, je voudrais, je devrais.

ex.en: In your place, I'd be careful.

rules.p: je voudrais softens a request, j'aimerais states a wish, and the conditionnel completes an unreal si-clause.

ex.en: I'd love to come, but I'm working.

rules.p: In reported speech and news, a past future becomes conditionnel: il a dit qu'il viendrait.

ex.en: She promised she would call.

rules.p: The conditionnel marks unconfirmed, second-hand information — the speaker isn't vouching for it. Constant in news.

ex.en: The suspect is reportedly on the run.

rules.p: que je parle, que je finisse, que je vende. nous and vous borrow the imparfait stem: que je vienne, que nous venions.

ex.en: You have to come.

rules.p: être → soit, avoir → ait, aller → aille, faire → fasse, pouvoir → puisse, savoir → sache, vouloir → veuille, valoir → vaille, falloir → qu'il faille, pleuvoir → qu'il pleuve.

ex.en: so that you're there.

rules.p: After je veux que, je suis content que, il est dommage que, c'est triste que, the next verb goes subjunctive.

ex.fr: Je suis ravi que tu sois là.
ex.en: I'm delighted you're here.

rules.p: il faut que tu fasses. With no second subject, keep the infinitive: il faut partir.

ex.en: We have to leave.

t61.exc: Certainty verbs go the other way: je sais que, il est clair que take the indicative.

rules.p: Subjective or uncertain triggers (il faut que, bien que, je doute que) take subjunctive. Stated as fact (je pense que, il est certain que) take indicative.

ex.fr: Je pense qu'il est là, mais je doute qu'il reste.
ex.en: I think he's there, but I doubt he'll stay.

rules.p: je pense que → indicative; je ne pense pas que → subjunctive. Negating an opinion plants doubt.

ex.en: I don't think she's coming.

rules.p: The thing becomes the subject: ce tableau a été peint par Picasso. par introduces the doer.

ex.fr: La souris a été mangée par le chat.
ex.en: The mouse was eaten by the cat.

rules.p: On + active verb does the same job and sounds normal: on a volé ma voiture.

ex.en: Someone stole my bike.

rules.p: Means 'by doing' or 'while doing'. The en-form shares its subject with the main verb, and the -ant never agrees.

ex.fr: Il apprend le français en écoutant la radio ; elles chantaient en marchant.
ex.en: He learns French by listening to the radio; they sang while walking.

rules.h: Form it from the nous form
rules.p: Drop -ons, add -ant: parler → en parlant, finir → en finissant. The odd ones: avoir → ayant, savoir → sachant.

ex.en: You learn by knowing how to listen.

rules.p: arriver → l'arrivée, développer → le développement. Formal writing prefers the noun version of an action.

ex.fr: La construction du pont a pris deux ans.
ex.en: The construction of the bridge took two years.

rules.p: utile → l'utilité, possible → la possibilité. -ité and -(t)ion do most of the work.

ex.en: It's of great use.

rules.p: The infinitive itself can be the subject or object where English uses the -ing form: mentir est mal, j'aime dormir.

ex.en: Lying is wrong.

rules.p: me te nous vous → le la les → lui leur → y → en. Il me le donne fits all three first slots.

ex.fr: Elle me l'a offert pour mon anniversaire.
ex.en: She gave it to me for my birthday.

rules.p: Positive commands attach the pronouns after the verb: donne-le-moi. Negative ones wrap as usual: ne me le donne pas.

ex.en: Give it to me!

rules.p: me, te, le, la shrink before y and en: m'y, t'en, l'y, l'en. And lui/leur never combine with y — one or the other.

ex.en: He's sending me there tomorrow.

rules.p: For anything the verb links with de: le livre dont je parle (parler de), la chanson dont il se souvient (se souvenir de).

ex.fr: le film dont tout le monde parle.
ex.en: the film everyone's talking about.

rules.p: Possession with de: la voisine dont le chien aboie. Whose, when the sentence runs on de.

ex.fr: un auteur dont les livres se vendent bien.
ex.en: an author whose books sell well.

rules.p: avec lequel, à laquelle, dans lesquels. lequel agrees in gender and number with what it replaces.

ex.en: the table I work on.

rules.p: After a preposition naming a person, qui does the job: l'ami avec qui je voyage.

ex.fr: un ami avec qui je voyage souvent.
ex.en: a friend I often travel with.

rules.p: quelqu'un, tout le monde, personne ne, rien ne, quelque chose, tout. personne and rien need ne.

ex.fr: Tout le monde est là, personne ne manque.
ex.en: Everyone's here, nobody's missing.

rules.p: quelque chose, quelqu'un, rien take de + adjective: quelque chose de beau, quelqu'un de gentil, rien d'intéressant.

ex.en: He/she is someone very kind.

rules.p: chacun = each one, quelques-unes = some (agrees), plusieurs = several, certains = some, d'autres = others.

ex.en: I've read a few of his books.

rules.h: When the whole clause is the object
rules.p: ce qui = what (subject of its clause), ce que = what (object), ce dont = what (after de).

ex.fr: Je sais ce que tu veux ; ce qui compte, c'est l'effort.
ex.en: I know what you want; what matters is effort.

rules.p: si + present in the if-half, future or present in the other half. Never a future after si itself.

ex.fr: Si tu veux, on ira à la plage.
ex.en: If you want, we'll go to the beach.

rules.p: si + imparfait → conditionnel in the other half. Unreal today, but still daydreamable.

ex.fr: Si j'avais le temps, j'achèterais une maison.
ex.en: If I had the time, I'd buy a house.

rules.p: The mistake everyone makes: si j'aurais. The if-half takes imparfait, only the other half gets the conditionnel.

ex.en: If I were you, I'd be careful.

rules.p: Present → imparfait, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, futur → conditionnel. 'Je pars' becomes il a dit qu'il partait.

ex.en: 'I'm arriving.' → She said she was arriving.

rules.p: Yes/no questions report with si. Wh-questions keep their word in statement order, no inversion.

ex.fr: Elle m'a demandé si je venais ; il a demandé où j'allais.
ex.en: She asked if I was coming; he asked where I was going.

rules.p: A command becomes de + infinitive after dire or demander. Negatives keep ne pas before the infinitive: elle nous a demandé de ne pas partir.

ex.fr: Il m'a dit de fermer la porte.
ex.en: He told me to close the door.

rules.p: que lands after the verb and limits it: je n'ai que cinq euros. Keep the ne in writing.

ex.en: Only two tickets are left.

rules.p: aucun + ne = not a single one; ni… ni = neither nor, with a single ne.

ex.en: I have neither the time nor the desire.

rules.p: comme opens the sentence (Comme il pleut, restons), puisque cites a known cause, car explains mid-sentence.

ex.en: Since you insist, I'll stay.

rules.p: donc, c'est pourquoi, c'est pour ça que all point forward to the consequence.

ex.fr: Il pleuvait ; c'est pourquoi on a annulé.
ex.en: It was raining; that's why we cancelled.

rules.p: pour que + subjunctive when a new subject acts; pour or afin de + infinitive when the subject stays. The same split runs through avant: avant de partir, avant qu'il parte.

ex.fr: Je parle lentement pour que tu comprennes ; avant de partir, ferme la porte.
ex.en: I speak slowly so that you understand; before leaving, close the door.

rules.p: Concede, then counter. bien que takes the subjunctive; même si takes the indicative.

ex.en: Although it's late, we carry on.

rules.p: Ce qui + verb + c'est + the star of the sentence. The star usually comes last, where the emphasis lives.

ex.en: What annoys me is the noise.

rules.p: For general statements about things: il est important de venir. Switch to c'est when you point at a specific one with a noun.

ex.en: It's important to arrive on time.

rules.p: un matin, soudain, puis, enfin, le lendemain. They pace the story; imparfait runs underneath, events land in passé composé.

ex.en: Suddenly, the light went out.

rules.p: Futur of avoir or être + participle: j'aurai fini, je serai rentré. For an action done before another future one.

ex.fr: Quand tu arriveras, j'aurai déjà mangé.
ex.en: When you arrive, I'll have already eaten.

rules.p: Inside a time clause, a future action that must complete first lands in the futur antérieur.

ex.en: When you've finished, call me.

rules.h: avoir or être + participle, as an infinitive
rules.p: après avoir mangé, après être rentré. Keeps the infinitive after a preposition while pointing at the past.

ex.en: After working, he sleeps.

rules.p: après être partis, après être partie. Same agreement rule as the passé composé.

ex.en: after coming back from the trip.

rules.p: The participle has its own past: ayant + participle, étant + participle. The action finished before the main one.

ex.fr: Ayant fini son travail, il est sorti.
ex.en: Having finished his work, he went out.

rules.h: The main clause sets the floor
rules.p: il dit qu'il viendra (present → future), il a dit qu'il viendrait (past → conditionnel). Each step back shifts the subordinate one step too.

ex.fr: Il a dit qu'il viendrait le lendemain.
ex.en: He said he would come the next day.

rules.p: demain → le lendemain, hier → la veille, aujourd'hui → ce jour-là.

ex.en: 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'; 'yesterday' → 'the day before'.

rules.p: With faire + infinitive, the participle stays frozen: les robes qu'elle a fait coudre.

ex.en: the furniture she had delivered.

rules.h: Pronominals with indirect objects don't agree
rules.p: elles se sont parlé, elles se sont téléphoné: parler à and téléphoner à make the object indirect, and agreement dies.

ex.en: They called each other last night.

rules.p: aurais or serais + participle: j'aurais dit, je serais venu. Pairs with si + plus-que-parfait for the past that never happened.

ex.en: If I'd known, I'd have come.

rules.p: With no si-clause at all, the conditionnel passé scolds or regrets — the hypothesis stays unspoken.

ex.en: You could have warned me!

rules.p: vouloir, douter, nier, craindre, éviter que + subjunctive. Impersonals follow: il est possible que, il vaut mieux que.

ex.en: I doubt he'll come.

rules.p: je suis sûr que, il est évident que, il dit que. But nier and douter stay subjunctive even though they sound certain.

ex.en: I deny that he lied.

rules.p: After le meilleur, le seul, le premier, le dernier, the subordinate verb often goes subjunctive.

ex.fr: C'est le meilleur film que j'aie vu.
ex.en: It's the best film I've seen.

t86.exc: Affirmative espérer que takes the indicative: j'espère qu'il vient. Only negated or questioned espérer leans subjunctive.

rules.h: Learn the gang as one block
rules.p: pour que, afin que, avant que, bien que, quoique, jusqu'à ce que, à condition que, à moins que, pourvu que, sans que, de peur que always take the subjunctive. No exceptions to weigh.

ex.en: Stay here until he comes back.

rules.p: après que describes something that already happened, so it takes the indicative: après qu'il est parti.

ex.en: after she got home.

rules.p: qu'il ait fini, qu'elle soit partie. The subjunctive action finished before the main one.

ex.en: I regret that she refused.

rules.p: The adjective describes (un professeur négligent), the participle acts (en négligeant sa santé).

ex.en: a careless teacher / by neglecting his health.

rules.p: excellent / excellant, précédent / précédant, convaincant / convainquant, différent / différant.

ex.en: a convincing argument.

rules.p: lequel, laquelle, lesquels, lesquelles choose between known options. With à and de they fuse: auquel, duquel.

ex.en: Which of these two sweaters do you prefer?

rules.p: si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé. Regret about the past that can't be redone.

ex.fr: Si nous étions partis plus tôt, nous aurions vu le coucher de soleil.
ex.en: If we'd left earlier, we'd have seen the sunset.

rules.p: Past condition, present result: si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel présent. The missed chance explains now.

ex.en: If you had studied, you would understand now.

rules.p: si also introduces indirect questions (je me demande si elle viendra), suggestions (si on allait au cinéma ?) and wishes (si seulement il était là !).

ex.en: What if we went to the cinema?

rules.h: Just in case vs only if
rules.p: au cas où takes the conditionnel (au cas où il pleuvrait); à condition que takes the subjunctive (à condition que tu viennes).

ex.fr: Prends un parapluie au cas où il pleuvrait.
ex.en: Take an umbrella in case it rains.

rules.p: quoique = although (quoique ce soit difficile). quoi que = whatever (quoi que tu fasses).

ex.en: Whatever you do, be careful.

rules.p: Even if, with a conditionnel in both halves: quand bien même tu refuserais, je comprendrais.

ex.fr: Quand bien même tu refuserais, je comprendrais.
ex.en: Even if you refused, I'd understand.

rules.p: de peur que + subjunctive = for fear that; non que + subjunctive = not that. Both formal.

ex.fr: Je me tais de peur qu'il se fâche.
ex.en: I stay quiet for fear he'll get angry.

rules.p: faute de + noun = for lack of; sous prétexte que = on the pretext that, usually suspicious.

ex.en: For lack of time, I gave up.

rules.p: il parla, il finit, il vendit, il fut, il eut. Lives in literature and formal history. Recognize it; you rarely need to write it.

ex.fr: Il fut une fois une princesse qui vécut seule.
ex.en: Once upon a time there was a princess who lived alone.

rules.p: il alla = il est allé, elle dit = elle a dit. Same meanings, older clothes.

ex.fr: Elle arriva à l'aube. (= elle est arrivée)
ex.en: She arrived at dawn.

rules.p: The passé simple of avoir or être + participle: the past right before a passé simple event. Purely literary, and almost always after dès que or quand.

ex.en: As soon as he had finished, he left.

rules.h: Agree unless the object is indirect
rules.p: elles se sont levées agrees. But se parler, se téléphoner, se plaire run on à, which makes the object indirect and kills the agreement: elles se sont parlé.

ex.en: They smiled at each other.

rules.h: A following direct object also blocks it
rules.p: elle s'est lavé les mains: les mains is the real object, the participle ignores it.

ex.en: She washed her hands.

rules.p: je pense que goes indicative, but je ne pense pas que flips to subjunctive. Same for il me semble que.

ex.fr: Je ne crois pas qu'il ait raison.
ex.en: I don't think he's right.

rules.p: crois-tu que, est-il possible que lean uncertain, so the subjunctive fits.

ex.en: Do you think she's coming?

rules.p: il est possible que (subjunctive) hedges; il est certain que (indicative) commits. Choose the mood first, the verb second.

ex.fr: Il est possible qu'il pleuve ; il est certain qu'il fait gris.
ex.en: It may rain; it's certainly grey.

rules.p: Before it happens, doubt: avant qu'il parte (subjunctive). After it happens, it's history: après qu'il est parti (indicative).

ex.fr: avant qu'il ne parte / après qu'il est parti
ex.en: before he leaves / after he left

rules.p: j'aurais une question, ce serait peut-être mieux, je voudrais comprendre. The conditionnel hedges an opinion or request in polished speech.

ex.fr: J'aurais une question, si vous permettez.
ex.en: I'd have a question, if you allow.

rules.p: croire savoir, prétendre avoir fini, sans hésiter. Formal French prefers an infinitive clause where speech would use que.

ex.en: He claims to have seen everything.

rules.p: After voir, entendre, regarder, écouter, sentir, the second verb stays an infinitive, never a conjugated form or a que-clause.

ex.en: I hear her singing.

rules.p: Eût-il su, il serait venu: an old subjunctive, inverted, replaces si. High literature only.

ex.en: Had he known, he would have come.

rules.p: A fossil meaning 'even if it were': je le finirai, fût-ce tard.

ex.en: I'll finish it, even if it's late.

rules.p: quelque + noun = a few (quelque temps); quelque + adjective = however (quelque difficile); quel que + être = whatever (quel que soit le prix).

ex.fr: Quel que soit le prix, je paie.
ex.en: Whatever the price, I'll pay.

rules.h: à and de fused into lequel
rules.p: auquel, duquel, auxquels, desquelles. For things, after verbs that need à or de: penser à, hériter de.

ex.en: the project I'm thinking about.

rules.p: l'ami avec qui reads warmer than l'ami avec lequel, though both exist.

ex.fr: un collègue avec qui je m'entends bien.
ex.en: a colleague I get along with.

rules.h: celui de, celle qui, le sien
rules.p: Replace a repeated noun with a demonstrative or possessive pronoun; it keeps the noun's gender.

ex.fr: Ma voiture ? C'est celle de ma sœur.
ex.en: My car? It's my sister's.

rules.p: avoir beau + infinitive: no matter how hard one tries, it fails. avoir conjugates like avoir.

ex.fr: Il a beau crier, personne ne l'entend.
ex.en: He can shout all he likes, nobody hears him.

rules.p: Both halves usually in conditionnel: quand bien même il pleuvrait, j'irais.

ex.en: Even if it rained, I'd go.

rules.p: ainsi = thus, en effet = indeed, or = yet (formal, nothing to do with 'or').

ex.en: Yet the situation had changed.

rules.p: toutefois, néanmoins (however); par conséquent, dès lors (therefore).

ex.fr: Le budget est faible ; néanmoins, on continue.
ex.en: The budget is small; nevertheless, we continue.

rules.p: Rarement ai-je vu, à peine est-il arrivé. Formal writing inverts after fronted adverbs like rarement, à peine, peut-être.

ex.en: Perhaps he'll come tomorrow.

rules.p: avant que tu ne partes, de peur qu'il ne pleuve. After certain subjunctive triggers an extra ne appears and adds no negation.

ex.fr: Je reste jusqu'à ce qu'il ne revienne.
ex.en: I'm staying until he comes back.

rules.p: il s'agit de = it's about, il convient de = it is fitting to, il importe de = it matters to. Formal texts dodge je and nous.

ex.fr: Il convient de signaler que le délai expire.
ex.en: It should be noted that the deadline expires.

rules.p: Spoken: on, ça, pas without ne, futur proche. Written: nous, cela, full negation, futur simple.

ex.fr: On n'y va pas ↔ Nous n'y allons pas.
ex.en: We're not going (spoken vs written).

rules.p: je parlai, tu parlas, il parla, nous parlâmes, vous parlâtes, ils parlèrent. The accented endings carry the tense.

ex.en: They spoke at length until dawn.

rules.p: je finis, nous finîmes, ils finirent; je vendis, nous vendîmes, ils vendirent. A circumflex marks the nous and vous forms.

ex.en: We sold the house the following year.

rules.p: With laisser + infinitive, agreement with a preceding object is now standard: les enfants qu'elle a laissés sortir.

ex.en: the children she let go out.

rules.p: These agree with a preceding object too: les risques qu'il a courus, la vie qu'ils ont vécue.

ex.en: the risks he ran.

rules.p: Imperfect subjunctive: stem + -asse, -asses, -ât, -assions, -assiez, -assent. Literature only; it maps one-to-one onto the present subjunctive.

ex.en: although it was late, they carried on.

t114.exc: Its past twin, the subjonctif plus-que-parfait (qu'il eût parlé), is effectively obsolete — the subjonctif passé does the job in modern French.

rules.p: Same meaning as j'aurais parlé. Identical in shape to the literary pluperfect subjunctive; very formal writing only.

ex.en: Had I known, I would have come.

rules.p: un grand homme = a great man, un homme grand = a tall man. Before the noun the adjective goes figurative; after it, literal.

ex.en: a great man ≠ a tall man.

rules.p: ancien (former vs antique), cher (dear vs expensive), propre (own vs clean), pauvre (poor soul vs penniless).

ex.en: my poor friend (alas) / a poor man (broke)

rules.p: nul ne = nobody (formal), ne… point = not at all (dated), ne… guère = hardly.

ex.en: No one is a prophet in their own land.

rules.p: Ce jardin, mon grand-père l'avait planté. Left-dislocation lifts the important thing to the head of the sentence.

ex.en: That garden, my grandfather had planted it.

rules.p: In description, trailing adjectives with commas weigh each one: une robe, verte, éclatante, impossible.

ex.en: a dress, green, dazzling, impossible.

rules.p: n'en déplaise à, somme toute, quitte à, il n'empêche que. You can't rebuild them from modern rules; learn them whole.

ex.fr: N'en déplaise à ses critiques, son œuvre demeure.
ex.en: Much to his critics' displeasure, his work remains.

rules.p: bagnole (casual), voiture (neutral), véhicule (formal). Pick one register per text and stay in it.

ex.en: jalopy / car / vehicle.
